canonical.name: Finite-free local minimality convention: a finite free resolution is minimal when every differential has image in the maximal ideal times the preceding free module
Koszul Betti-number convention: the degree-i exterior rank is the i-th rank in the minimal Koszul resolution

sources.title: Miles Reid, notes by Alexandros Groutides, Commutative Algebra II, Chapter 5: Koszul complex, regular sequences
sources.locator: Contents/title page and Chapter 5 `Koszul complex and regular local rings`: Definitions 5.1-5.4, Theorem 5.1, Corollaries 5.2-5.3, Theorem 5.4 and Corollary 5.5 (PDF pp. 1-4); heading `5.1 Hilbert's syzygy theorem` and Theorem 5.6; then Section 5.2 `Regular local rings`, Definitions 5.5-5.6, Lemma 5.7, Corollary 5.8, Lemma 5.9, and Theorems 5.10-5.11 (PDF pp. 5-7).

contents.name: Chapter 5 `Koszul complex and regular local rings`
Theorem 5.1 (Kunneth formula for Koszul homology)
contents.reason: The source's Kunneth formula introduces a separate homological tensor-product computation. This pair only needs the explicit signed concatenation isomorphism and its one-element cone consequence, both proved directly without importing the Kunneth package.

contents.name: Section 5.2 `Regular local rings`
contents.reason: This section begins the regular-local-ring development. Its embedding-dimension, associated-graded, and homological-characterization results are the scope of the planned CA-18 page, not this finite Koszul-complex pair.

contents.name: Definition 5.5 (embedding dimension)
contents.reason: Embedding dimension is needed to define and test regular local rings, but it is not used in the Koszul acyclicity route. The downstream CA-18 page builds that invariant before applying it to minimal resolutions.

contents.name: Definition 5.6 (regular local ring)
contents.reason: The regular-local condition combines dimension with embedding dimension and belongs to the later CA-18 subject. This page uses only the explicitly stated Noetherian-local hypotheses for its regular-sequence converse.

contents.name: Lemma 5.7 (dimension inequality and equality for a regular sequence)
contents.reason: This dimension comparison is one of the regular-local-ring tools used downstream to relate parameters to dimension. The present page proves Koszul acyclicity, not the dimension theory of regular local rings.

contents.name: Corollary 5.8 (dimension drops by the length of a finite-module regular sequence)
contents.reason: The corollary compares regular-sequence length with finite-module dimension, which is a depth and Cohen--Macaulay invariant statement. CA-17 receives the regular-sequence input from this page and develops that comparison.

contents.name: Lemma 5.9 (quotient of a regular local ring by independent cotangent classes)
contents.reason: This quotient-regularity lemma depends on the regular-local and cotangent-space framework. It is required by the later CA-18 regular-local-ring development, but not by any Koszul construction or local acyclicity proof here.

contents.name: Theorem 5.10 (a regular local ring is a domain)
contents.reason: The theorem is a structural consequence of regular local rings and needs their dimension and prime-avoidance arguments. It has no proof role in the present ordered-regular-sequence and Koszul-homology scope.

contents.name: Theorem 5.11 (regularity iff the associated graded ring is polynomial)
contents.reason: This associated-graded characterization is central to the downstream regular-local criterion, while this page deliberately stops after minimal Koszul resolutions and their exterior ranks without developing associated graded rings.

sources.title: Mircea Mustata, Commutative Algebra
sources.locator: Table of contents (PDF pp. 2-3); Section 11.1 `Regular sequences and depth`, Definition 11.1, Remarks 11.2-11.3, and Proposition 11.4 (book pp. 100-102); and Section 11.3 `The Koszul complex`, the defining paragraphs, Lemma 11.43 through Exercise 11.53 (book pp. 110-114).

contents.name: Theorem 11.52
contents.reason: This result identifies depth through the maximal length of regular sequences. The next CA-17 page owns depth and Cohen--Macaulay modules; this page supplies the regular-sequence input but deliberately does not introduce depth invariants.

contents.name: Exercise 11.53
contents.reason: This exercise introduces perfect modules through projective dimension and depth, then associated-prime consequences. Neither perfect-module theory nor the required projective-dimension package belongs to this Koszul page; the current plan does not assign that exact result a dedicated destination.

sources.locator: Section 15.29 `The Koszul complex`, Definitions 15.29.1-15.29.2 and Lemmas 15.29.3-15.29.12 (HTML section, all named results).

contents.name: the explicit differential formula following Definition 15.29.1
Lemma 15.29.9
contents.reason: This product-of-two-elements cone refinement is not needed for the finite Koszul route here. Powers are proved from ordinary regularity after adjacent swaps, so importing this separate homotopy-equivalence construction would add unused machinery.

contents.name: Lemma 15.29.10
contents.reason: This is the Koszul specialization of the preceding product-cone refinement. The page uses the one-element cone sequence and direct exterior concatenation instead, so this additional homotopy-equivalence theorem has no proof role.

contents.name: Lemma 15.29.11
contents.reason: This exact sequence for a product entry is a useful refinement of the product-cone analysis, but it is not required for acyclicity, the local converse, or the stated power closure. Adding it would duplicate a mechanism not used by this page.
